scenes.title: Environment Variables & PATH
scenes.narration: Environment variables are named values your shell and programs read to decide how to behave, and PATH is the most important one of all.

scenes.title: Why They Matter
bullets: They configure programs without changing code, like pointing to a database with DATABASE_URL.
They keep secrets such as API keys out of your source files.
The PATH variable tells the shell which folders to search for commands you type.
scenes.narration: Environment variables let you tweak how software runs without touching a single line of code, which is why a setting like DATABASE_URL lives there. They are also the standard place to hold secrets like API keys so they never get committed to a repository. Above all, the PATH variable defines the list of directories the shell scans to find the programs you invoke.

scenes.title: Working with Variables
scenes.code:
echo $HOME                # read a variable
export API_KEY="abc123"   # set for this session
echo $PATH                # see the search folders
export PATH="$PATH:/opt/bin"  # add a folder
scenes.narration: You read a variable by prefixing its name with a dollar sign, as in echo $HOME. The export command sets a variable so child programs can see it too. When you print $PATH you get a colon-separated list of folders, and the last line shows the common trick of appending a new directory while preserving the existing ones.

scenes.title: How the Shell Finds a Command
scenes.narration: When you type a command, the shell does not search your whole disk. Instead it checks each folder listed in PATH, in order, until it finds a matching program and runs it. This is why a fresh install sometimes reports command not found until its folder is added to PATH.

scenes.text: To make variables permanent, add your export lines to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc so they load in every new shell.
scenes.narration: Variables set with export vanish when the terminal closes. Put your export lines in a startup file like ~/.bashrc to make them stick across sessions.
